given: a warehouse operator is filing a stock record for a SKU at a location
when: the filed quantity is below zero
then: the filing is rejected with a clear message that names the quantity field, and no stock record is created or changed
architectural_notes: Verified at the JSON boundary (app/routes/): a negative quantity is rejected before any persistence, so no row is created or changed. Realizes defence-in-depth for non-negative stock (R2/NFR-F1-2) — the boundary/service guard produces the field-naming validation message (NFR-F1-6, owned at the boundary), while the PI3 CHECK (quantity >= 0) is the DB backstop. Cross-cutting: input validation owned at the API boundary, never the domain. Covered by the real-branch pytest-bdd suite asserting both the rejection and that stock_records is unchanged.

rationale: This asserts the write-time rejection of a negative quantity with a field-naming message, an outcome independently breakable from the happy-path create (AC1) and the collision update (AC2): an implementation can persist and update correctly yet still accept a negative quantity or reject it with an unnamed error.
